notes: Wilson Audio official WATT / Puppy Series 8 technical specifications page: two 8-inch woofers (20.32 cm), one 7-inch midrange and one 1-inch inverted titanium dome tweeter (driverCount 4 counts transducers). Sensitivity is published as '92 dB @ 1 watt (2.83V at one meter)'; stored as 1W/1m because the manufacturer states the 1 W reference explicitly, and the 2.83 V wording is retained here for transparency. Nominal impedance 4 ohms, minimum 3 ohms. Frequency response +0/-3 dB 21 Hz - 22.5 kHz is the manufacturer's average in-room response and is not a free-field or anechoic limit. Minimum amplifier power (7 W per channel) is not a recommended or continuous power rating and is not stored. No power handling, response points, or directivity are published on this page and none are imported. Source: https://www.wilsonaudio.com/products/watt-puppy/watt-puppy-series-8.

notes: Secondary technical specification: hi-fi+ review of the Focal Kanta N°2 floorstanding loudspeaker (2024). Revision note: the hi-fi+ review describes the current Kanta N°2 and the record does not name a production run, so no earlier-revision values are transferred. Driver complement per the review: 1 x 27 mm IAL3 beryllium inverted dome tweeter, 1 x 165 mm flax midrange with TMD, 2 x 165 mm flax woofers (driverCount 4). Sensitivity 91 dB at 2.83 V / 1 m; nominal 8 ohms with 3.1 ohm minimum; recommended amplifier power (40-300 W, per other sources) is a range and is not stored. Crossover 260 Hz - 2.7 kHz. Woofer size is the 6.5-inch (165 mm) LF driver. Not verified against the Focal manufacturer page, which was not located in the research pass. Source: https://hifiplus.com/articles/focal-kanta-no-2-floorstanding-loudspeaker/.

UNAVAILABLE - the Thiel CS2.4 has at least two documented production runs with different published specifications, and the catalog row does not name one. Stereophile's specification sidebar (https://www.stereophile.com/content/thiel-cs24-loudspeaker-specifications) describes units reviewed with serial numbers from 1991 and 1992 (8-inch woofer, 8.5 x 11-inch passive radiator, 4 ohm nominal / 3 ohm minimum, 87 dB/2.83V/m, 36 Hz-25 kHz +/-2 dB, recommended power 100-400 W). AudioWorld's 2003 announcement of the 'new CS2.4' describes a different coincident-driver design with a 7.5 x 11-inch passive radiator and a -3 dB bandwidth of 33 Hz-37 kHz (https://audioworld.com/music-tech/2003/thiel-cs2-4-loudspeaker/). Because the revision cannot be established, no values from either run are transferred and all physical fields remain N/A. Catalog ID preserved. Source for the revision conflict: the two URLs cited above.

UNAVAILABLE - the catalog row says 'IN-8' without a generation. MartinLogan official Motion Series brochure for the Motion 40: 40-25,000 Hz +/-3 dB; sensitivity 92 dB @ 2.83 volts/meter (stored as 2.83V/1m, the dataset's existing reference label for the same 2.83 V at 1 m measurement); 4 ohms nominal, compatible with 4/6/8 ohm amplifiers; crossover 500 and 2,600 Hz; drivers: 1 x 1 in x 1.4 in folded Motion tweeter, 1 x 5.5 in aluminum midrange, 2 x 6.5 in aluminum-cone woofers (driverCount 4 counts transducers; woofer value is the 6.5-inch driver). Recommended amplifier power 20-300 W is a range and is not stored as a scalar. Dispersion 80 x 80 degrees is a published coverage angle and is not a polar dataset. The later Motion 40i listings share these figures; they are not transferred to a separately-named record and no 40i-specific values are imported. Source: https://www.martinlogan.com/uploads/documents/brochures/brochure_motion40.pdf.

notes: Secondary copy of the Mackie HR624 (original, not MK2) owner's manual, hosted by ManualsLib: active 2-way, bi-amplified studio monitor with a 6.7-inch (170 mm) die-cast LF driver and 1-inch titanium/aluminum HF dome, plus a rear passive radiator (not counted as a driver).
